title: Concatenated Divisibility
summary: Given an array of positive integers and a positive integer k, find the lexicographically smallest permutation of the array such that the concatenated number is divisible by k.
statement: Given an array of positive integers and a positive integer k, find the lexicographically smallest permutation of the array such that the concatenated number is divisible by k. If no such permutation exists, return an empty list.
constraints: nums has at most 13 positive integers and k is at most 100.
Permute every occurrence, concatenate decimal representations, and require divisibility by k.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid integer list, or [] when none exists.
hints: A partial permutation is fully described by its used-index mask and current remainder.
Memoize whether each state can reach remainder zero, then reconstruct by trying remaining values in ascending order.
Append value with (remainder*10^digits+value)%k; choose the first candidate whose next state is feasible.
The DP explores every indexed permutation, while greedy reconstruction over feasible blocks produces the smallest value sequence, including duplicates.
editorial: The DP explores every indexed permutation, while greedy reconstruction over feasible blocks produces the smallest value sequence, including duplicates.

tests.explanation: Both [3,12,45] and [12,3,45] work; the first is lexicographically smaller.
Only concatenation 510 is divisible by ten, so the answer is [5,10].
